title: Add SLOs for Private backup job success + restore drill latency (with burn-rate alerts)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Introduce SLO definitions + burn-rate alerting hooks for Private Day-2 backup job success and automated restore drill latency; adds standard labels/suppression guidance for maintenance windows.
description: Title: Add SLOs for Private backup job success + restore drill latency (with burn-rate alerts) Context: As part of the Private Day-2 backup/restore + DR readiness work, we need first-class SLOs that can be consumed by SRE + on-call automation (and mirrored into customer-facing dashboards where applicable). This PR adds SLO definitions and standard burn-rate alerting hooks for: (1) backup job success rate and (2) automated restore drill latency. These SLOs are intended to be used by Redwood SRE for Redwood-managed Private environments and as reference defaults for customer deployments running our observability pack. Goals: - Provide consistent SLI/SLO definitions with clear scopes/labels - Wire standard multi-window burn-rate alerts (fast + slow) - Avoid noisy paging for non-prod while preserving signal for prod/private - Document assumptions + required metrics emitting behavior Dependencies/related work: - Metrics emission: redwood PR-24344 (structured metrics around backup/restore) - Dashboards/alerts: observability-pack PR-94 (visualization + alert routing) - Backup/restore automation: redwood-private-installer PR-482 / PR-489; helm chart CronJob PR-131; restore drill automation ENG-9827 SLOs included: 1) Backup job success (Private control plane) - SLI: error ratio over job runs, measured from counter redwood_backup_job_runs_total{env="prod",deployment="private",component="control-plane",status=~"success|failure"} - Objective: 99.5% successful backup runs over a 28d rolling window (allows for transient storage/KMS issues while still pushing us to harden) - Notes: This is a job-based SLO (not request-based). We explicitly exclude manual test runs and include scheduled CronJob runs only via label job_type="scheduled". We also include a short grace for deployments during maintenance windows via a documented suppression label. 2) Restore drill latency (Private staging + periodic prod drill) - SLI: proportion of drills completing within threshold AND latency distribution; the SLO uses a latency-based SLI derived from redwood_restore_drill_duration_seconds_bucket and redwood_restore_drill_runs_total. - Objective: 95% of restore drills complete in <= 45 minutes over a 28d rolling window - Secondary indicator (non-SLO but charted): p95 restore drill duration in seconds over the last 7d for operational tuning - Notes: By default, restore drills are expected to run in staging (to validate tooling without impacting customers). For prod/private environments where customers opt in to periodic drills, we use the same SLO definition but default alert routing is “ticket” unless deployment label enable_paging="true" is set. Alerting strategy: - Burn-rate alerts for backup success: - Fast burn: 2h / 6h windows, page if burning > 14x (aligned with other job SLOs) - Slow burn: 1d / 3d windows, page if burning > 3x - Burn-rate alerts for restore drill latency: - Ticket on slow burn by default (staging), page only when enable_paging="true" - Includes explicit “no data” handling: if no drill has run in the expected schedule window, we emit a separate warning alert (restore_drill_missing) to catch cron/scheduler failures. What changed: - Added new SLO spec files under slo/private/ for: backup_job_success and restore_drill_latency - Added reusable recording rules for job-based error ratio and restore drill latency SLI - Added burn-rate alert templates + routing annotations (severity, runbook, owner) - Updated README with label requirements, maintenance window suppression guidance, and example PromQL queries Files (high level): - slo/private/backup_job_success.yaml - slo/private/restore_drill_latency.yaml - recording_rules/private_backup_restore.rules.yaml - alerts/private_backup_restore_burnrate.yaml - alerts/private_restore_drill_missing.yaml - README.md (Private Day-2 section) - tests/promql_lint_test.go (adds fixtures for new rules) - fixtures/prometheus_rules_expected.txt (updated golden) Example PromQL snippets: - Backup success rate (28d): sum(rate(redwood_backup_job_runs_total{env="prod",deployment="private",component="control-plane",status="success",job_type="scheduled"}[28d])) / sum(rate(redwood_backup_job_runs_total{env="prod",deployment="private",component="control-plane",job_type="scheduled"}[28d])) - Restore drill <=45m (ratio): sum(rate(redwood_restore_drill_runs_total{env="prod",deployment="private",result="success",duration_le="2700"}[28d])) / sum(rate(redwood_restore_drill_runs_total{env="prod",deployment="private"}[28d])) Rollout notes: - These SLO configs are safe to ship and consume immediately, but require the metrics from redwood PR-24344 (or equivalent) to avoid “no data” conditions. README calls this out explicitly. - For existing environments with legacy metric names, we intentionally did not add compatibility shims in slo-toolkit; compatibility mapping should live in the metrics emission layer or the observability pack. Testing: - promtool check rules (CI) - Unit tests for rule generation + golden fixtures - Manual validation against staging Prometheus with synthetic series (see README commands) Checklist: - [x] SLO definitions reviewed with SRE (Sean/Neha) - [x] Alert severity + routing aligns with on-call policy (no default paging for staging) - [x] Runbook links added (placeholders pointing to Confluence until public docs are live) - [x] Label taxonomy documented (env/deployment/component/job_type/enable_paging) - [x] CI green

review_conversation: Allison Grant (Observability): The label taxonomy looks right, but can we ensure the SLO scope is strictly Private control plane? I’m worried we’ll accidentally include dedicated/hosted metrics if labels drift. Also, please add explicit annotations for owner + runbook so downstream tooling can route correctly. Sergio Costa (author): Good call. I tightened matchers to deployment="private" and component="control-plane" for the backup SLO and added requiredLabels docs. Added owner=eng-sre and runbook annotations in both alert groups. Sean Gallagher (SRE): Burn-rate thresholds: 14x fast burn is fine for paging, but restore drill alerts shouldn’t ever page by default. We’ve had staging drills flap due to resource pressure. Can we make paging opt-in? Sergio Costa: Updated restore drill burn-rate alerts to severity=warning + route=ticket by default, and added enable_paging="true" gate for paging. Also added restore_drill_missing as warning to catch schedule failures without waking people up. Neha Kapoor (Reliability): For backup jobs, please add a small “for:” to avoid paging on a single scrape gap or one-off job failure. Also, what’s the plan for maintenance windows? Sergio Costa: Added for: 15m to fast burn and for: 1h to slow burn. Documented maintenance suppression via alertmanager silence + optional label maintenance_window="true" propagated by the env overlay (README). Rafael Mendes (Game day owner): The 45m threshold is OK for reference deployments, but we should call out that on-prem NFS backends may be slower. Ensure the doc states this is a default and can be tuned. Sergio Costa: Added README note about tuning restore threshold per environment and recommended baselining during first game day. Allison Grant: Approved after tightening matchers and adding annotations. Sean Gallagher: Approved with opt-in paging change. Neha Kapoor: Approved.
